questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of the Osculating Circle
questions.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(-1,-\pi )$ where $t=\pi $, given that $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖=\pi ,$ and the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(\pi )=⟨-1,-\pi ⟩$,  since the point $P(-1,-\pi )$ is at the tip of $r(\pi ).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$, ${T}^{′}(\pi )$ and $‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩=⟨0,1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖}{‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖}=\frac{\pi }{1}=\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=\pi $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\pi ) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖}=⟨0,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\pi )+R(\pi )N(\pi ) & =⟨-1,-\pi ⟩+\pi ⟨0,1⟩=⟨-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: The center is $(-1,-\pi )$ and the radius is $\pi $
The center is $(-1,-2\pi )$ and the radius is $\pi $
The center is $(-1,0)$ and the radius is $1$
The center is $(-1,0)$ and the radius is $\pi $
The center is $(-1,-2\pi )$ and the radius is $1$

answer_fields.correct_value: The center is $(-1,0)$ and the radius is $\pi $

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Radius of Curvature Using the Cross Product Formula
questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨{cos}^{3}⁡t,{sin}^{3}⁡t⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({cos}^{3}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{3}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨-3{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,3{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨-3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}),3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})⟩ \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}⟨-1,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}\cdot \sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{cos}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{sin}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡t{sin}^{2}⁡t-3{cos}^{3}⁡t,\,6\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t-3{sin}^{3}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨6\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}){sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-3{cos}^{3}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}){cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-3{sin}^{3}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨6(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}){(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{3},6(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}){(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{2}-3{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})}^{3}⟩ \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}⟨1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =(\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4})⟨-1,\,1,\,0⟩\times (\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4})⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & ={(\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4})}^{2}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \,-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{9}{8}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}\,-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-\frac{9}{8}\cdot 2\,k \\  & =-\frac{9}{4}\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}=\frac{{(\frac{3}{2})}^{3}}{\,\frac{9}{4}\,}=\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=4$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨4\sqrt{t-3},t-1⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(4)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(4)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\sqrt{t-3}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{2}{\sqrt{t-3}},1⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(4) & =⟨2,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(4)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{t-3}}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{\sqrt{(t-3)^{3}}},0⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(4) & =⟨-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(4)$ and ${r}^{″}(4)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(4)\times {r}^{″}(4) & =⟨2,1,0⟩\times ⟨-1,0,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(4)\times {r}^{″}(4)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the radius of the osculating circle at  $t=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(4) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(4){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(4)\times {r}^{″}(4)‖}=\frac{(\sqrt{5})^{3}}{\,1\,}=5\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨t,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨1,-\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{tan}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-{sec}^{2}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨0,-{sec}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,-2,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-2\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖} \\  & =\frac{(\sqrt{2})^{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{2} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of the Osculating Circle
questions.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(3,1)$ where $t=0,$ given that $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖=2,$ and the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨-\frac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}},\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(0)=⟨3,1⟩,$ since the point $P(3,1)$ is at the tip of $r(0).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$, ${T}^{′}(0)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{t}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{\sqrt{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{3}}},\,\frac{t}{\sqrt{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{3}}}⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =⟨-\frac{1}{\sqrt{{({0}^{2}+1)}^{3}}},\,\frac{0}{\sqrt{{({0}^{2}+1)}^{3}}}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{2}{1} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=0$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=⟨-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)+R(0)N(0) & =⟨3,1⟩+2⟨-1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨3,1⟩+⟨-2,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: The center is $⟨3,2⟩$ and the radius is $1$
The center is $⟨1,1⟩$ and the radius is $2$
The center is $⟨-1,1⟩$ and the radius is $2$
The center is $⟨3,3⟩$ and the radius is $2$
The center is $⟨2,1⟩$ and the radius is $1$
